A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaM-SLidE study. Their complete 46-page documents, including Appendices A–H, provide readable and matchable text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: V4 reports original LaM-SLidE trajectory-prediction results in Tables 1–5 and original scaling, reconstruction and identifier experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: V5 retains these original benchmark results and appendix experiments, alongside baseline results attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The entity identifiers, cross-attention encoder/decoder, latent flow model, two-stage training and task-specific objectives remain unchanged (Section 3; Appendices B, C and E).

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same ETH-UCY scenes, NBA rebounding/scoring scenarios, three N-body systems, eight MD17 molecules and tetrapeptide trajectories. No training or evaluation coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables, including human-motion baselines, GeoTDM and its joint-molecule MD17 comparison, and MDGen with the MD-replicate baseline.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, conditioning/prediction horizons, metrics, model sizes and training/inference settings are unchanged (Sections 4, E and G; Tables 7–12).

E4.justification: The model-size, function-evaluation, latent-count, identifier-pool, random-assignment and attention-pattern analyses are retained unchanged in Section 4.7 and Appendix G. Appendix H visualizations also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain five-run reporting for N-body and MD17 and standard-deviation error bars over five random identifier assignments in Figures 7–8. No statistical procedures or run/seed disclosures change.

E6.justification: Main and appendix result entries, numerical values and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, LaM-SLidE's aspirin ADE/FDE remains 0.059/0.098 in Table 4; the scaling tables and reconstruction plots also match.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.2, Propositions 3.3–3.4 and their Appendix F proofs are unchanged, as are the dynamical-system equations, stochastic-interpolant mathematics and loss definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about entity traceability, fixed-size latent representations, performance across domains and scalability.

C2.justification: The compression–prediction tradeoff, identifier-retrieval explanations, scaling interpretations and qualifications concerning graph foundation models remain unchanged (Sections 5, D.2 and G).

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, pseudocode, hyperparameters, software/hardware disclosures and code/data access information are unchanged. Repaired internal references point to technical material already present in v4.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix D and the cited works are unchanged. The positioning relative to GNNs, latent generative models and graph foundation models remains the same.

P1.justification: V5 repairs unresolved references to Appendices B, E and G, standardizes appendix figure/table/algorithm references, updates affiliation 4 and reorders acknowledgments. These are limited editorial changes without substantive restructuring.

P2.justification: Edited references produce minor text reflow and small spacing shifts in Appendix B's algorithm blocks. Figures 1–17 and Tables 1–16 retain their content, captions, numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: V5 replaces broken appendix references in Sections 3.3, 4 and 4.6 with clear pointers to existing architecture, implementation and supplementary evidence. This provides a limited readability and navigation improvement; the scientific content and supporting results remain unchanged.
